capabilities.does: A signed-in person bids on a live or scheduled auction lot, with an optional proxy maximum. The system bids for them up to the maximum, one increment over the next highest maximum, and extends the close if the leader changes inside the soft-close window.

address.how: the Place bid button of the bid box (packages/commerce/src/components/BidWidget.tsx, wired in app/lots/[id]/page.tsx)

capabilities.open: Read carefully (2026-11-16). GOOD: one transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the lot row, so two bids on a lot are serialised; the amount is only an input, the minimum is recomputed server-side from the lot ladder; closed, not-yet-open and ended lots are refused; the leader is read inside the lock. CONCERNS: (1) no seller check anywhere: the maker or store member can bid on their own lot (shill bidding); placeBid never compares bidderId with the artwork store or maker. (2) the action never passes clientIp/userAgent to placeBid, so the audit columns bid.client_ip and user_agent are always null for human bids. (3) amounts are rounded but not checked for finite numbers: NaN or Infinity from a crafted call reach the INSERT and fail there (transaction rolls back, a 500, no bad row), so harmless but untidy; no upper cap on a maximum. (4) the card on file only gates the first bid; nothing charges it. The winner gets an order with 72 hours to pay and is never auto-charged, and there is no penalty for a non-payer other than the order lapsing. (5) no rate limit on bids. (6) SOFT-CLOSE LIKELY UNDONE FOR SERIES LOTS: tickAuctionClock.applySeriesSchedule rewrites auction_lot.end_at from the series live_at (or closes_at_override) every 30 s for scheduled and live lots whenever it differs, and placeBid stores the soft-close extension only in end_at. So an extension would be reverted at the next tick and the lot settled at the original time despite last-minute bids. Not tested on data; confirm with the series auction-clock owner.

address.how: the Buy now for {price} button in the bid box (packages/commerce/src/components/BidWidget.tsx, wired in app/lots/[id]/page.tsx)

capabilities.open: Read carefully (2026-11-16). GOOD: lot row locked FOR UPDATE; refused after the first bid, with no buy-now price, or when the piece is not available. CONCERNS, weaker than placeBid: (1) no end_at check: a lot past its end time but not yet settled (settle runs on page views and the 30 s clock) can still be bought now. (2) no card-on-file requirement, unlike placeBid, so anyone signed in can take a lot. (3) no seller check (a seller can buy their own lot). (4) buy-now is allowed on a scheduled lot before it opens (may be intended). (5) the lot is marked sold in one transaction and the order is created afterwards outside it; if the process dies between the two, the lot stays sold with no order; the failure path puts the lot back to live unconditionally (not "scheduled" if it was, and not conditional on it still being sold). (6) the payment due is 72 hours, hard-coded in buyNowLot and settleExpiredLots rather than marketplace_settings.paymentWindowHours.

capabilities.open: The conditional UPDATE (status IN awaiting_etransfer, payment_received, pending_payment) makes a double confirm impossible. CONCERN: pending_payment is the unpaid CARD state, so a store manager can mark a pending Stripe order paid as eTransfer without any money arriving (the studio host also rewrites payment_method to etransfer), which accrues the maker's balance. SECURITY: the wiki is network-wide and these cases check only that a viewer is signed in (forum-ui actions.ts:307-377). wiki-archive calls archiveWikiPage(id) with no viewer or role (services wiki.ts:381-400: UPDATE threads SET status archived WHERE id AND kind wiki_page), and wiki-update and wiki-revert pass the viewer id only as the editor name (revertWikiPage wiki.ts:360-378): any account, however new, can archive any wiki page and overwrite or revert any other (revisions are kept, but archiving hides the page). apps/forum/src/lib/connectors.ts supplies wiki.* with no role wrapper, so the network host is where this is reachable. Same finding as the sunjay and amrit rows; wiki-update has an optimistic lock (expectedUpdatedAt).
elktours (elktours-forum-wiki-edit): Seven wiki cases (wiki-define, wiki-talk, wiki-create, wiki-update, wiki-archive, wiki-revert, line) share one capability; the case bodies were not read past the action names. Role rules live in the forum service.
amrit-canada (amrit-forum-wiki-edit): SECURITY: packages/forum-ui actions.ts handles wiki-archive (line 347), wiki-update and wiki-revert after checking only viewer.userId; archiveWikiPage(id) takes no viewer or org (services wiki.ts:381, UPDATE threads ... WHERE id AND kind = wiki_page). The wiki is network-wide (listWikiPages is unscoped). So any signed-in account, including a follower of this site, can archive or overwrite any network wiki page by id, through /api/forum/wiki-archive here. Same on every app that mounts this route.

capabilities.open: Good: whole card in one transaction; photos must be this org's, of type image, and not already attached to a card; coordinates plausibility-checked; rubric points frozen only at rating. CONCERNS: (1) rate limit is checked at the start and recorded only after success, so parallel requests all pass the check and can exceed the limit. (2) getClientIp trusts the FIRST x-forwarded-for hop; unless the proxy overwrites the header, a client can spoof the IP and dodge the IP bucket (guest and user buckets still apply, and a guest id is a cookie the client can drop). (3) the photo check does not tie the media row to the poster, so a caller who learns an unattached media id (nanoid, 21 chars, hard to guess) could attach someone else's upload. (4) cards publish immediately and anonymously to PUBLIC by design (migration 077); the only control is a report and a takedown. (5) getViewer errors are swallowed (.catch null), so an auth outage posts as a guest.

capabilities.label: Add, edit, stop or remove an address in an org's book
capabilities.does: Pastes addresses into an org's contacts (skipping anyone who unsubscribed), edits a contact's name, tags and notes, writes an unsubscribed row for an address the org was asked to stop mailing, or deletes a manual contact.
capabilities.why: Nobody has recorded where this is done yet.
capabilities.next: Find where it is done and record the page in the atlas.
capabilities.status: a contacts row for (org, email) with the status, name and tags
capabilities.open: GOOD: org scoping is in every WHERE; an unsubscribed address is never revived by a paste (CASL) and is reported back. SECURITY (consent): addAddresses inserts pasted addresses as status `new`, source `manual`, with no record that the person consented; the newsletter list (listRecipients: status <> unsubscribed) then mails them. A paste is the org's own claim of consent, but nothing stores who asserted it beyond added_by. A concurrent paste of the same address can hit the unique index and throw (the select-then-insert race), failing the batch mid-way after earlier rows were written. tags are stored as sent (no length or count cap).

capabilities.open: SECURITY: `html` is stored and later sent to every recipient exactly as saved (only the unsubscribe footer is added); no sanitising here, so any script-like markup an editor pastes is mailed (email clients strip most, not all). Concurrent saves lose one (read then write). saveNewsletter merges sentAt/sentCount from the previous read, so a save that races a send can reset the sent record.

capabilities.label: Send a letter to the list (or three test addresses)
capabilities.does: Renders the letter per recipient with an unsubscribe footer, emails every recipient (org contacts minus unsubscribed, or a series' subscribers) one by one through sendEmail, and records sentAt and sentCount on the letter.
capabilities.why: Nobody has recorded where this is done yet.

capabilities.status: site_config value.sentAt and sentCount on the letter; email_sends rows kind newsletter
capabilities.open: SECURITY: (1) no send guard: sendNewsletter does not look at sentAt, take a lock or claim a row, and the hidden-enneagram route calls it with no sent check at all, so a double click, a retry or two tabs mails everyone twice (only ifac and innergathering have a `force` flag, which implies a guard in their routes; the package does not provide one). sentAt is stamped after the whole loop. (2) The send is one HTTP request that mails recipients serially, so a long list can outlive the request or a proxy timeout partway, with no resume; a partial send stamps sentCount but the next send goes to everyone again. (3) `force` skips the broken-link and placeholder check. (4) baseUrl, which builds the unsubscribe links, comes from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL or the request Host header in the routes: with the variable unset a forged Host header changes where the unsubscribe link in real mail points (editor-only action). (5) Recipients are re-read at send time, so a suppression written by pkg-email-events-ingest between preview and send is honoured (good).
